findings.problem: Unchecked arithmetic: `start + len as usize` uses plain `+` which wraps silently in release mode and panics in debug mode. No explicit overflow handling via `checked_add`, `saturating_add`, or `wrapping_add`.
findings.failure_mode: In release builds, overflow silently wraps to a small value, producing an out-of-bounds slice that then panics on line 4. In debug builds, it panics immediately on overflow. Either way, overflow behavior is unobservable to the caller and unhandled.
findings.fix: Use `start.checked_add(len as usize).ok_or(Error::Overflow)?` and propagate a typed error instead of letting overflow silently wrap or panic.

findings.problem: Unchecked range indexing: `&buf[start..end]` performs runtime bounds checks and panics if `start > buf.len()` or `end > buf.len()`. No validation of `offset`, `len`, or computed bounds before indexing. Caller-supplied `u32` parameters are cast to `usize` and used directly without proof of bounds.
findings.failure_mode: Any `offset` greater than `buf.len()` or `offset + len > buf.len()` causes a panic. Malicious or erroneous input (e.g. `offset=0, len=u32::MAX`) will always panic. This is a denial-of-vector surface and violates the panic-free production standard.
findings.fix: Validate bounds before slicing: `if start > buf.len() || end > buf.len() { return Err(Error::OutOfBounds); }` or use `buf.get(start..end)` and return `Option`/`Result` instead of panicking.

findings.problem: Function returns `&[u8]` directly with no error type, meaning any failure (overflow, out-of-bounds) must panic. The return type cannot encode failure, violating the checked-returns principle that callers must be able to handle failure without panic.
findings.failure_mode: The only way for this function to signal failure is to panic. There is no `Result` or `Option` in the signature, so the caller has no recoverable path.
findings.fix: Change signature to return `Result<&[u8], Error>` or `Option<&[u8]>`, define an error type with variants like `OutOfBounds` and `Overflow`, and validate all inputs before producing the slice.

findings.problem: Function is 3 logical lines and passes the size rule, but has zero invariant checks. No parameter validation exists despite `offset` and `len` being externally supplied `u32` values with no constraints.
findings.failure_mode: No defense-in-depth: any caller can trigger a panic with valid-looking but out-of-range inputs.
findings.fix: Even in a short function, add explicit boundary validation before the arithmetic and slicing operations.

findings.problem: No `rust-toolchain.toml` present. The crate uses edition 2021 with no pinned nightly toolchain.
findings.failure_mode: Without a pinned toolchain, builds are non-reproducible and may silently change behavior across toolchain updates.
findings.fix: Add a `rust-toolchain.toml` with a pinned dated nightly channel if nightly features are needed, or document stable-only usage.

findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that fixes for overflow and bounds do not regress performance; no measurement baseline exists.
findings.fix: Add a `cargo bench` benchmark targeting `read_window` with varied `offset`/`len`/`buf` sizes to establish a latency baseline before and after fixes.

findings.failure_mode: Unverified: cannot confirm the compiled code performs zero redundant bounds checks on the hot path.
findings.fix: Run `cargo asm --lib review_arithmetic_indexing::read_window` or `cargo llvm-ir` on the fixed version to verify bounds-check elimination.

residual_risk: Static review only. The function has three BLOCKER-class violations: unchecked arithmetic (wrapping/panic), unchecked indexing (runtime panic on out-of-bounds), and a return type that cannot express failure (only panic). These are not subtle — they are immediate panic surfaces on untrusted input. Without the fixes (checked arithmetic, bounds validation, Result return type), any call with malicious or malformed parameters will panic. No commands were run per the review-only scope; actual clippy, test, and benchmark execution is required before acceptance.
